conceptual.anchor: The architecture now looks like this ... RAW INPUTS → Evidence → Identity/Lineage/Dependency/Context/Validity → Evidence Graph → Assessment Calculus ρ → Evidence Assessment → Conclusion / Conflict → Knowledge State → Zero/Lord/Sarathi ... the calculus is a replaceable policy component.

formal.anchor: First axiom: determinism ... EA_\rho(E,P,C)=EA_\rho(E,P,C) ... The same evidence, context and policy must produce the same assessment. If an LLM happens to produce different results each time, that variability cannot be hidden inside the mathematical definition. It must be represented as InferenceUn

rationale_evidence.anchor: Now test candidate mathematics ... Maximum ... Avoids duplicate inflation ... Cannot represent cumulative corroboration well ... Mean ... Simple ... Duplicate-sensitive; dilution problems ... Weighted sum ... Flexible ... Weights become policy assumptions ... Bayesian ... Requires priors, likelihood
rationale_evidence.statement: Compares nine candidate aggregation frameworks (Maximum, Mean, Weighted sum, Saturating aggregation, Bayesian, Dempster-Shafer, Possibility theory, Argumentation frameworks, Graph-based evidence models) against strengths/problems, concluding there is probably no single universal KnowledgeOS evidence algebra — a Kernel + Pluggable Assessment Calculi architecture is mathematically stronger.
